_comment: Structured site data the MCP apps render from. Mirrors content/*.md (real facts). Edit freely — no rebuild needed.

projects.name: nibli
projects.desc: Zero-hallucination symbolic reasoning engine — a hallucination firewall for the LLM era. Lojban in, first-order logic out; a proof trace on every conclusion. (Zero-hallucination = inference soundness, not premise truth — like Lean.) Live demo at /nibli — the real engine in your browser.

projects.name: botwork
projects.desc: Single-binary Rust automation framework for acceptance testing and RPA — plain-text human-readable syntax, extensible via Rust, Python, and JavaScript. A faster, lighter take on Robot Framework.

projects.name: dhilipsiva.dev
projects.desc: This website — a Zola static site that ships its own AI: the LoRA fine-tuned twins you're talking to, plus the live nibli engine, all in-browser via candle Rust→WASM. Open source, training pipeline included. A quine of a website.

projects.name: webapp-checklist
projects.desc: The technical details a programmer should consider before making a web app public. The most-starred thing I've shipped (~366★) — proof that the most useful artifact can be a list.

projects.name: awesome-programmer
projects.desc: Resources to learn from and become a self-taught awesome programmer (102★) — the dropout's path, written down for the next one.

projects.name: hostscli
projects.desc: Python CLI that blocks and unblocks websites straight from /etc/hosts. A small utility, not a flagship — sometimes the best firewall is a text file.

projects.name: cognito
projects.desc: Pure-Rust System 2 reasoning kernel — a failed experiment in a transformer that thinks in explicit steps. The premise survived; the execution didn't. Kept public because failure is data; the lessons moved into nibli.

projects.name: awesome-rust-ml
projects.desc: A curated map of the Rust machine-learning ecosystem. Curation is also building: someone has to keep the index honest.

projects.name: garuda
projects.desc: Automagically exposes the Django ORM over gRPC, so microservices in any language can use it. Niche, useful, very 2018 — there was a talk.

projects.name: email-template-generator
projects.desc: Responsive, maintainable, unified email templates for Sendgrid, Mandrill & co — SASS, Pug, one common layout (30★).

projects.name: orm-choices
projects.desc: Helpful decorators + utils for choice fields — Django choices or SQLAlchemy ChoiceType. Do choices the pythonic way.

projects.name: style.js
projects.desc: A layman's tool to style HTML elements and share CSS values — built to end the UI back-and-forth with non-technical clients.

projects.name: STGI
projects.desc: Technical Architect, since May 2026 — backend engineering for niche tech initiatives. The newest chapter.

projects.name: NuFlights
projects.desc: Principal Architect (2023–26) on the airline-retailing platform I originally built at Reckonsys — including rewriting the NDC adapter from Python to Rust (async-graphql, sea-orm).

projects.name: Colligence Research
projects.desc: Principal Architect, Distributed Systems/Rust (2023–25). First MVP of a distributed WebRTC media server in Rust; Pulumi infrastructure-as-code end to end.

projects.name: Appknox ×2
projects.desc: 2014–17: architected the mobile-security scanning platform from scratch, built the team 1→5, ran an iOS/Android device farm. 2022–23: a Rust microservice generating CycloneDX SBOMs from mobile binaries — no source required.

projects.name: Nitimis
projects.desc: CTO for five years (2018–23), non-profit ethos: RobotFramework QA services, and teaching people with zero tech background to start QA-automation careers — unpaid, on purpose.

projects.name: the Reckonsys years
projects.desc: VP of Engineering (2019–22), ~70% hands-on by choice. Django/GraphQL/React for startups, teams of 2–10; open-sourced 'bigga' and the cookiecutter templates everything was scaffolded from.

projects.name: ReWire
projects.desc: An iOS mindfulness app (2012, at Tataatsu) — meditation and attention training, with an API for scores and leaderboards. A one-person team, end to end.

about.tagline: An Optimistic Nihilist who loves Science, Rust, Python, FOSS, WebAssembly, WebRTC, Web3, Distributed Systems, and symbolic reasoning.
about.bio: Hands-on software architect, lifelong builder. Bangalore, India. I care about correctness, freedom, and code that still makes sense in a decade. Not an entrepreneur — I just want to build the things.
